fact_text: Power-sector circular debt was reported at about Rs 2.3 trillion in FY24 and about Rs 1.6 trillion in FY25.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Circular debt fell in FY25 mainly because the government made large stock payments to power producers, using fiscal space and extra subsidies, and renegotiated some IPP contracts after terminating others.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Under-recoveries and distribution losses of distribution companies totalled about Rs 1.7 trillion over roughly the four years to FY25.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Distribution losses run at about Rs 300 to 400 billion a year, which the reporter called a time bomb if they are not addressed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: An IMF structural benchmark requires privatising distribution companies and generation companies; the reporter argued distribution losses can fall materially only after that privatisation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government is reprofiling about Rs 660 billion of debt owed by Pakistan Holding Power Limited, moving it to Central Power Purchasing Guarantee Limited instead of raising new debt.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Interest on the reprofiled debt moves from KIBOR plus 45 bps to KIBOR minus 90 bps, a saving of about 1.35 percentage points and roughly Rs 13 billion over six years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government is raising about Rs 615 billion of new debt from conventional and Islamic banks at KIBOR minus 45 bps, an effective cost of about 10.1 percent, and 18 banks have signed the agreement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: New circular debt is serviced by a debt service surcharge of Rs 3.23 per kWh on electricity bills, capped at about 10 percent of the NEPRA revenue requirement.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: At KIBOR around current levels the debt service surcharge would repay the new debt in about six years, and faster if KIBOR falls below about 10 to 11 percent, according to the reporter's estimate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The debt service surcharge is already collected in electricity bills, so it adds no new charge to consumers, and it ends once the debt is repaid.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government's power-sector circular debt resolution package is about Rs 1.3 trillion, of which the late-payment surcharge owed to IPPs is the most contested part.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government aims to bring circular debt to zero; if fiscal space is limited, the reporter said the stock could still stay around Rs 300 to 400 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government has paid Chinese-linked IPPs about 92 percent of amounts billed over roughly nine to ten years up to August 2025, a total of about Rs 5.5 trillion, with payment often delayed but made.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government owed Chinese-linked IPPs about Rs 423 billion at the time of the video, of which about Rs 230 billion was capacity payments and Rs 16 to 20 billion energy payments.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Port Qasim Electric, China Power Hub Generation and one other Chinese-linked IPP account together for about Rs 70 to 80 billion of the amounts owed to Chinese-linked IPPs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The government first said it would not pay the late-payment surcharge owed to Chinese-linked IPPs, and those IPPs said they would not waive it, so the dispute over the surcharge remains open.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter said waiving the late-payment surcharge would set a precedent, so other IPPs would then seek similar relief on their own dues.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: Chinese-linked IPPs asked for a revolving account so that any dues are released immediately; the reporter said immediate release would put pressure on foreign exchange reserves.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter said a surcharge waiver could come with tougher conditions, such as higher return on equity on upfront tariffs, so the deal would be harder to close than the government expects.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter thinks the late-payment surcharge may be paid in stages over time, possibly through a promissory note, rather than upfront.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter said fiscal consolidation, meaning lower government spending, could free extra funds to pay IPPs beyond the amounts already planned.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter expects the power-sector circular debt resolution to proceed, possibly with delays of a few weeks, because the structure is plain and all banks have signed, with the IMF on board.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The prime minister was reported to travel to China for a Shanghai conference at the end of August 2025, where renegotiation of power-sector dues might be discussed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: PSO's current trade debts were reported at about Rs 437 billion and its short-term borrowing at about Rs 355 to 360 billion, with IPPs owing it about Rs 66 billion in trade debts.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: PSO's share price was about Rs 400 at the time of the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter argued PSO is the main listed beneficiary of power-sector circular debt resolution, since IPP trade debts owed to it would be paid, which could support a re-rating.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: RLNG-based power companies owe about Rs 90 to 100 billion in trade payables; the reporter assumed PSO handles 70 to 80 percent of RLNG, so about 77 percent of those payables would reach PSO, roughly Rs 100 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter said the per-share effect on PSO could be substantial, but the exact figure is uncertain because amounts and settlement timing are unclear.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: The reporter said refinery and exploration companies would be minimal beneficiaries of the power-sector debt reprofiling.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)

fact_text: For gas circular debt, the reporter named OGDC and Pakistan Petroleum as the major expected beneficiaries of the government's planned resolution.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Will the Circular Debt Finally Be Resolved? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-08-25)
